children: The Financial Times has reported that while the radical left in the U.S. captures public attention, moderates are set to dominate the incoming U.S. Congress following the recent midterm elections. This outcome follows the November 3, 2026, elections where Democrats gained control of both the House and Senate. The report highlights that most of the newly elected Democratic lawmakers are moderates, which could influence legislative priorities and political dynamics in the coming term. The Democratic Party's performance in the elections saw a notable shift in several Republican-held Senate seats, yet the party's overall composition remains moderate.
The Financial Times report suggests that the influence of the radical left in the new Congress may be more about visibility than actual legislative power.
Market pricing appears consistent with a potential decrease in confidence in Democrats achieving a significant popular vote margin, as moderate candidates gain prominence.
The Democratic Party's moderate composition may influence its legislative strategy, aligning more with centrist policies.

Watch for how the Democratic Party's moderate majority will shape its legislative agenda and whether this impacts the party's standing in the 2026 midterm popular vote markets. Key actors such as House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries and President Donald J. Trump may play significant roles in upcoming legislative negotiations. As results continue to be certified, any shifts in the vote margin could influence market perceptions of Democratic strength in upcoming elections.

title: Moderates to dominate incoming US Congress after 2026 elections: FT
